newsitem.title: USA: Firefighters battle big California blaze.
newsitem.headline: Firefighters battle big California blaze.

text.p: Firefighters battled on Friday to hold back a fast-growing wildfire in California's scenic Los Padres National Forest, officials said.
About 1,500 firefighters were fighting the blaze, which broke out on Monday evening and has swelled to 5,600 acres (2,270 hectares), a national forest spokesman said.
The fire, in a rugged, inaccessible area, was only 10 percent contained and there was no estimate of when it would be fully contained, the spokesman said.
Helicopters scooped huge buckets of water from the nearby Pacific Ocean and dumped them on the fire burning along a mountain ridge, he said.
The fire is burning just south of Big Sur, a picturesque area on the California coast popular with hikers and campers.
Officials suspect arson as the cause of the fire, which is located about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.

One home, four outbuildings and one vehicle were confirmed lost, the spokesman said. The fire has been moving inland, away from populated areas, but has encroached on backwoods areas of the Fort Hunter Liggett army base, officials said.
Another wildfire near Vacaville, 60 miles (100 kms) northeast of San Francisco, was fully contained by Friday evening, California Department of Forestry spokeswoman Alleah Haley said.
The 1,520-acre (615-hectare) brushfire, which started on Wednesday, was expected to be fully controlled by Saturday evening.
A 15-year-old boy has been charged with starting the blaze as well as several other fires. He denied the charges during a court appearance in nearby Fairfield on Friday.
